newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW - Brazil's Itau to rest after latest buy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Brazil's Itau to rest after latest buy.

text.p: Banco Itau, Brazil's second-largest private bank, said its purchase last week of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj puts an end to a prolonged buying spree.
"Now we are in a period of consolidation," Itau President Roberto Setubal told Reuters in an interview. "We are not interested in buying other banks for now."
Itau's acquisition of Banerj last week was the latest of a series of buyouts and ventures that began in 1993, with the opening of a subsidiary in Europe.

Itau opened a branch in neighboring Argentina in 1994. It then bought Banco Frances e Brasileiro (BFB), which belonged to French bank Credit Lyonnais and last year created a joint venture with U.S. Bankers Trust to focus on capital markets and investment banking.

Just several months before Banerj's acquisition, it took over its sister company Itau Seguros and bought the European branch of failed Banco Bamerindus in Luxembourg to strengthen its private banking operations in the region.
The Banerj purcahse took Itau's assets to 37.7 billion reais, placing it just 1.5 billion reais shy of Bradesco, Brazil's largest private bank with about 39 billion reais in assets.

Itau bought the bank for 311.1 million reais, slightly above the minimum price of 310 million reais. But Itau will pay for the state bank with privatization bonds that were acquired at a 50 percent discount.
Setubal said Itau was willing to pay more for Banerj if necessary. But Itau was the only bidder for the bank in the closed-envelope auction last Thursday.

He thinks that lingering concerns over Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts discouraged the other three likely buyers, Bradesco, BCN and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, represented by local Banco Pactual.
Rio de Janeiro state government had to ask for a 3.09 billion real loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) to cover the bank's pension and payroll-related debts.
"We were entirely satisfied with the guarantees provided by the state," he said.
Setubal said Itau bought Banerj because of its large client portfolio and its strong presence in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil's third economy.
"Our interest was in the bank's 700,000 clients and its presence in the state," he said.
Banerj adds 193 branches to Itau's network of about 650 branches in the state of Rio.
Setubal said Rio has committed itself to keeping its accounts at the bank for at least five years. Most of the bank's clients are state employees.
Itau's president also said the bank aims to modernize Banerj by investing in technology and offering clients a large number of products.
